name: Claude Code screen reader mode
description: A setting in Anthropic's Claude Code command-line tool that shows its work as plain labeled lines, numbered menus and yes-or-no prompts a screen reader can follow.

name: GitHub Copilot CLI
description: GitHub's AI coding agent for the terminal; it detects a screen reader by itself, labels its icons, turns off animations and accepts dictation.

name: OpenAI Codex CLI
description: OpenAI's coding agent for the terminal; it detects a screen reader at start-up and turns off animations, but it has no plain-text mode.

name: Gemini CLI screen reader setting
description: Google's coding agent for the terminal has a screen reader setting that shows plain text; a reported screen reader cursor bug was closed without a fix in May 2026, and since June 18, 2026 it no longer answers free, Google AI Pro or Ultra accounts (paid API keys still work).

name: Visual Studio Code
description: Microsoft's code editor; in 2026 it added offline dictation and a terminal accessible view, and its Agents window has accessibility help on Alt+F1.

name: Cursor
description: An AI code editor; version 3.23 made screen readers announce the highlighted item in the agent's / and @ menus. Older forum posts from blind users, whose dates could not be confirmed, said the agent panel was very hard to use with NVDA and JAWS.

name: Lovable
description: An AI website builder that published a 2026 accessibility statement aiming at WCAG 2.2 AA; it is not clear whether that covers the builder itself or only its website.

name: BlindPilot
description: A desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and other coding agents and splits each answer into rows you move through with arrow keys; note that every agent runs with permission checks off by default.

name: Claude Code Reader
description: A desktop window around the Claude Code command-line tool, built with native controls; its README says it was tested with VoiceOver, NVDA and JAWS.

name: Earshot for Claude Code
description: A Claude Code plugin that detects your screen reader, gives each answer whole instead of streaming it, and says "Still working" every 10 seconds.

name: Willow
description: A narrator that speaks only checked facts while a coding agent works: files changed, tests passed or failed, and when it is waiting for your permission.

name: Accessible Claude Code (Joseph Webber)
description: A web client for Claude Code that speaks its activity through live regions, sounds and a voice; an early version built by a blind developer, so far tested only with VoiceOver on the author's Mac.

name: agentaloud
description: A Windows app that runs Claude Code or Codex and shows the conversation as a read-only transcript with single-letter jumps, speaking through NVDA.

name: Claude Desktop stable feed
description: A workaround script that keeps the whole Claude Desktop conversation loaded so JAWS and NVDA stop jumping while you read; made by a blind JAWS user.

name: agent-ally
description: Speaks a coding agent's permission prompts aloud and lets you answer them by keyboard or from your phone.

name: Orca-Voice
description: Dictate into Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode and hear the answers read aloud.

name: screen-readers-mcp
description: Lets an AI agent press keys in a real NVDA, capture its speech and braille, and ask you when it is stuck, so add-ons are tested the way users hear them.

name: Accessibility Agents
description: A package of accessibility skills for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI and Antigravity that blocks edits to user-facing files until an accessibility review.
maintainer: Community Access (Taylor Arndt and Jeff Bishop)

name: claude-watch
description: Tells you when a Claude Code session is waiting for you; made by a blind developer.

name: HomerDev
description: A kit of C# and Python parts and templates for keyboard-first Windows apps, written so you can point an AI at it.

name: A11ySkills
description: A collection of 175 accessibility skills for AI coding agents, gathered from 8 public collections.

name: aria-first
description: React components for five hard web patterns (accordion, tabs, live regions, dialog, combobox), documented with what screen readers actually announce; built by a blind software engineer.

name: a11y-field-notes
description: A coding-agent skill listing web patterns that pass the rules but fail on real screen readers, checked by a blind VoiceOver user; not tested with TalkBack or NVDA.

name: NVDAStudio
description: An NVDA add-on where an AI agent creates, tests and packages other NVDA add-ons, with an accessibility check; its instructions are in Portuguese.

name: AI Content Describer
description: An NVDA add-on that describes the focused item, the whole screen or a camera picture with an AI model you choose, including a fully local option that needs no API key.

name: ChatGPT Companion
description: An NVDA add-on that reads new ChatGPT answers and progress updates without moving your focus.

name: VisionMate
description: An NVDA add-on for image descriptions that works fully offline with no account or API key; it downloads about 1.5 GB of vision data.

name: Luma
description: An NVDA add-on that connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter or an on-device model.

name: LIMA AI
description: An NVDA add-on that describes the screen or an element on request and can click an element you describe.

name: Kindlead
description: An NVDA add-on that uses Gemini to turn Kindle books into accessible web pages with headings.

name: Learning Python with NVDA
description: An NVDA add-on with 40 chapters for learning Python, with optional help from Gemini.

name: Padronix
description: An NVDA add-on that formats citations in APA, MLA, IEEE, Vancouver or ABNT style using an AI model.

name: VOCR
description: A VoiceOver companion for Mac that reads screens with text recognition, describes images with an AI model you choose, and can let the AI operate apps for you.

name: Be My Eyes
description: An app that connects you with sighted volunteers or AI to describe what your camera sees; it also works with Meta glasses.

name: Seeing AI
description: Microsoft's camera app that reads text, describes scenes and recognises products; the May 2026 Android version needs fewer TalkBack swipes.

name: Envision
description: An app and smart glasses that read text and describe scenes; Envision says scene description now runs on the phone itself, while its partner Arm calls this a prototype.

name: PiccyBot
description: An app that describes photos and videos. A podcast interview in April 2026 said smart-glasses support was in beta; the research could not confirm it is available.

name: Aira Explorer
description: Connects you to a trained human visual interpreter through your phone or Meta glasses; the Play listing mentions 60 free minutes.

name: Guided Vision in Gemini Live
description: Google's live camera descriptions in Gemini on Android, with spoken framing tips and follow-up questions; Google says it is not a mobility aid.

name: ProgramAT
description: Lets blind and low-vision people create their own camera-based tools by describing them in words; needs an iPhone 12 or newer, a GitHub Copilot subscription and a server.

name: STEM-ACCESS
description: Turns a PDF into a screen-reader-friendly web page, with maths as MathML, charts as data tables and diagrams as descriptions written by Claude.

name: Mubsir
description: A Windows assistant: hold a key and ask in Arabic or English, and it reads, explains and acts on the screen beside NVDA; it needs Anthropic and Google AI Studio keys.

name: QuickMail
description: A screen-reader-first Windows email client for Gmail, Outlook, iCloud and IMAP, over 90 percent written with AI by a long-time screen reader user.

name: QUILL for All
description: A family of screen-reader-first writing apps for Windows, with AI help from QUILL's own free AI, your ChatGPT subscription or your own Gemini key.

name: DualPen
description: A self-hosted editor where blind and sighted people write together, with sounds for who is typing where and a key to jump to a collaborator.

name: FastSMRW
description: A fast Mastodon and Bluesky client for blind users, rewritten in C++ for Windows.

name: Skills for the blind
description: Korean-first agent skills that help a screen reader user read, shorten, hear and dictate documents with Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity; made by a blind author.

name: py-maidr
description: A Python library that makes matplotlib, seaborn, Plotly and other charts explorable by keyboard, sound, braille and text.

name: maidr-skill
description: Teaches AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Copilot to make accessible MAIDR charts automatically.

name: maidr-mcp
description: Meant to show accessible charts inside ChatGPT or Claude that you explore with arrow keys, speech, sound and braille; experimental, and its makers say it is not yet checked in claude.ai or ChatGPT.

name: tablefmt
description: Rewrites Linux table output, such as ps and df, as name and value pairs so a screen reader reads each value with its column name.

name: AccessCaster
description: Controls a RODECaster Pro II or Duo from a keyboard-friendly web page instead of RODE's own app; built and used with NVDA by a blind podcaster.

name: ElevenLabs TTS Studio
description: A desktop app for ElevenLabs text-to-speech with a searchable voice list, made for NVDA, JAWS and Narrator users by a blind developer.

name: FFT Channel Vocoder
description: A command-line audio vocoder built by a blind programmer and musician.

name: Omni Describer
description: A Windows app where Gemini writes audio descriptions for a video, you review and edit them, and the app mixes them into the video; in maintenance mode.

name: Piper voice training guide
description: A guide, also usable by an AI agent, for training your own Piper text-to-speech voice on an ordinary computer without a graphics card.

name: Plexible
description: A desktop Plex media client for screen reader users, described by its author as vibe coded.

name: Voice of the Old Republic
description: A mod that makes Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic playable with a screen reader, built by a blind developer with help from Claude.

name: Civ V Access
description: A mod that makes Civilization V playable with a screen reader; F2 speaks AI-written descriptions of the artwork.

name: Blindfold for Balatro
description: A screen reader mod for the card game Balatro.

name: FFVIII Accessibility Mod
description: Makes the Steam edition of Final Fantasy VIII playable with speech; its 104 video descriptions were written by AI and not checked by people.

name: SpeechBridge
description: Lets you play Windows games with a screen reader on a Mac; built by a blind developer and an AI.

name: UnseenGodot
description: Six add-ons that make the Godot game editor usable with a screen reader, with tutorials.

name: SkyrimCK-MCP
description: Lets Claude Code read and write Skyrim mod files without opening the inaccessible Creation Kit; built for blind modders.

name: AccessSlice
description: A 3D-printing slicer with labelled pages and spoken slice reports, tested with NVDA, that works without internet.

name: OpenSCAD Assistive Forge
description: A browser tool for customising 3D models with screen reader support, including a braille card designer that translates on your own device.

name: Blockly for LEGO
description: A keyboard and screen reader block editor for LEGO SPIKE Prime; not yet tested on real hardware or by daily screen reader users.

name: Glide
description: A self-steering guide device for walking; pilot users began receiving units in 2026.

name: NVDA
description: The free, open-source screen reader for Windows; version 2026.1 moved to 64-bit and broke older add-ons, and 2026.2 added a built-in magnifier.

name: Vox
description: A new open-source screen reader for Windows 11, built with an AI agent workflow; still in testing.

name: acter
description: A Windows terminal where each command becomes a heading, so you move through a session like a web page; made by a blind software engineer. It is new: planning was finished and building had just started in 2026.

name: NexusShell
description: A Windows terminal that speaks the selected item in command-line menus for NVDA, JAWS and Narrator.

name: term-a11y
description: Replacements for terminal spinners, progress bars and tables that print plain text when a screen reader is in use, plus a checker.

name: rcdo
description: Screen reader and braille friendly summaries of Terraform, Ansible, AWS and gcloud output, written by an operator who is 90 percent blind.

name: Blind Vibe Coding directory
description: A link-checked list of tools, guides and communities for building software with AI without sight, with notes on the evidence for each.

name: Blind Apps directory
description: A list of 97 apps made by 40 blind or low-vision developers, 18 of them built with AI help.
